For release: after 8:00 p.m. 
Monday, September 21, 1980 


YMCA ANNUAL MEETING 
FEATURES CONFRONTATION 


Challenging samplings of how human realities are now being faced 
were dispensed Monday evening, prior to the 118th annual meeting of the 
Montreal YMCA. 

Visitor participation was high as an imaginative variety of techniques 
was used to disclose specifics--with interpretations--of the Y's multi- 
faceted role today. 

"The survival of our nation depends on the survival of our cities,” 
R.G. Rogers,the Montreal Y's general secretary, told a massed audience of 
government, industry and community representatives at the gathering. 

He deplored the tendency to over-rely on governments and insisted; 
"Our very heritage...depends on the individual taking the initiative." 

Such initiative, in turn, should lead to partnerships that would 
make most effective use of resources and avoid duplication, while involving 
local people in the affairs of their communities. 

In reviewing current Y activities, Mr. Rogers said they are relatively 
clear-cut in such fields as physical development, leadership training, 
recreation and continuing education. 

"But growing involvement with efforts to re-shape the community 
are less tangible, more volatile, less predictable and more difficult 
to manage."
